title: Aggregated External AI & Tech News
description: Merged headlines from configured external sources

items.title: Critical Copilot vulnerability allowed hackers to steal 2FA code from users (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: SearchLeak exploit shows why the industry's approach to LLM security fails over and over.

items.title: Users cry foul after AMD stripped memory crypto from its consumer CPUs (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: AMD's stripping of TSME from consumer CPUs appears to be a deliberate, covert move.

items.title: PeopleSoft 0-day affecting hundreds of organizations steals gigabytes of data (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Vulnerability in the Oracle-owned PeopleSoft software is about as critical as they come.

items.title: Locked in heated rivalry with researcher, Microsoft fixes 0-day they disclosed (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: A separate zero-day also disclosed by Nightmare Eclipse appears to be patched as well.

items.title: High-severity vulnerability in Linux caused by a single faulty character (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Use-after-free bug can be exploited to evade sandbox defenses.

items.title: For the 2nd time in weeks, Microsoft packages laced with credential stealer (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: 73 packages run self-replicating stealer as soon as they're opened by an AI agent.

items.title: How a USB-connected speaker can infect a PC without ever being touched (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Seller of the Sound Blaster Katana V2X doesn't consider the behavior a vulnerability.

items.title: Dashlane explains how attackers managed to download encrypted password vaults (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: By targeting large numbers of users, attackers increased their chances of success.

items.title: Can't make sense of Dashlane's vault theft notification? You're not alone. (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Security advisory leaves out key details. Dashlane maintains complete silence.

items.title: Dozens of Red Hat packages backdoored through its official NPM channel (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Anyone who has downloaded affected Red Hat packages should investigate immediately.

items.title: Botnet of more than 17 million devices dismantled (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: The botnet was reportedly tied to a Russia-based residential proxy network.

items.title: Fed up with vibe coders, dev sneaks data-nuking prompt injection into their code (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Undisclosed addition in jqwik instructed AI coding agents to delete app output.

items.title: Websites have a new way to spy on visitors: Analyzing their SSD activity (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Telltale SSD activity can be measured in the browser using simple JavaScript.

items.title: Millions of AI agents imperiled by critical vulnerability in open source package (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: "BadHost" was found in Starlette, a package with 325 million weekly downloads.

items.title: US's big bet on quantum computing may not be entirely legal (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Deal also launched the first quantum foundry company, but is there a need for it?

items.title: Texas AG sues Meta over claims that WhatsApp doesn't provide end-to-end encryption (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Critics note a lack of factual support in lawsuit filed by US Senate candidate.

items.title: A hacker group is poisoning open source code at an unprecedented scale (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: GitHub is just the latest victim of TeamPCP, a gang that has carried out a spree of software supply chain attacks.

items.title: US government takes $2 billion equity stake in nine quantum computing firms (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Beneficiaries include startup backed by firm with links to the Trump family.

items.title: Google publishes exploit code threatening millions of Chromium users (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: Google publishes exploit code before patch, reported 42 months earlier, is fixed.

items.title: In stunning display of stupid, secret CISA credentials found in public GitHub repo (Source: feeds.arstechnica.com)
items.content_text: SSH keys, plaintext passwords, other sensitive data had been up since November 2025.
